problem_statement: When an mDNS responder answers a host-name (A/AAAA) query, or a DNS-SD responder answers a service instance PTR query, the response advertises only a single IPv4/IPv6 address for the interface, even when the interface has several valid addresses configured. RFC 6762 (address queries) and RFC 6763 (DNS-SD additional records) require that all valid addresses on the sending interface be included, so a querier can choose among them; the current behaviour can even omit an address entirely. A responder should include every valid A/AAAA record for the interface in its response (best effort when the buffer is small), rather than a single pre-selected address.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/lib/mdns_responder -s tests/net/lib/mdns_responder/net.mdns -s net.mdns -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The task is solvable, but the statement must specify the changed public DNS-SD signature, NULL/unspecified/duplicate address behaviour, and the observable response count/order requirements checked by the tests.

problems.detail: The DNS-SD hidden tests call dns_sd_handle_ptr_query with a leading NULL/struct net_if * argument, but the statement does not specify the updated public API signature or parameter order.

The tests rely on observable behaviour that a NULL iface adds no interface-wide records, that explicitly supplied addr4/addr6 are ignored when NULL or unspecified, and that the supplied address is not duplicated when enumerating interface addresses; the original statement only says to include all valid addresses.

The hidden tests check exact response header counts and ordering: mDNS address responses must have ancount equal to the number of written A/AAAA answers, and DNS-SD PTR responses must keep TXT/SRV before the appended A/AAAA additional records and include those records in arcount.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase 'when enumerating the interface addresses they must be treated as already included so the same address is not added twice' hints at an implementation detail rather than just the observable requirement that the same address must not appear twice.
leak_check.suggested_statement: When an mDNS responder answers a host-name (A/AAAA) query, or a DNS-SD responder answers a service instance PTR query, the response advertises only a single IPv4/IPv6 address for the interface, even when the interface has several valid addresses configured. RFC 6762 (address queries) and RFC 6763 (DNS-SD additional records) require that all valid addresses on the sending interface be included, so a querier can choose among them; the current behaviour can even omit an address entirely. A responder should include every valid A/AAAA record for the interface in its response (best effort when the buffer is small), rather than a single pre-selected address. For the DNS-SD path, the public API dns_sd_handle_ptr_query must be updated to receive the network interface on which the query was received as its first parameter: int dns_sd_handle_ptr_query(struct net_if *iface, const struct dns_sd_rec *inst, const struct net_in_addr *addr4, const struct net_in6_addr *addr6, uint8_t *buf, uint16_t buf_size). A NULL iface means no additional interface-wide records are added, but the function still processes the explicitly supplied addr4 and addr6. Those explicitly supplied addresses should be advertised only when they are non-NULL and not unspecified, and the same address must not be advertised twice. For an mDNS A/AAAA host-name query, the response should contain one answer record for each valid address of the queried family (IPv4 for A and IPv6 for AAAA) on the sending interface, with distinct addresses and a DNS header answer count equal to the number of answer records actually written. For a DNS-SD service instance PTR response, the existing service additional records should remain in their current order, and the remaining A/AAAA additional records should be appended after them (for example after TXT and SRV records), with the DNS header additional-record count including the address records actually written. In both cases, collecting address records is best effort: if there is not enough remaining buffer space for another record, stop without failing.
